pages.headline: Real or pretend?
pages.deck: This month: how to check a picture, a game of real or pretend, and a detective kit for anything you see online.

art.alt: Night over the Guided Planet, with the space station crossing the sky and Bloop on the hill, thinking.

pages.headline: Welcome back, explorers

letter.text: This month is all about one question: is it real, or is it pretend? Pictures, videos and stories can be made by people, by computers, or by both, and it is not always easy to tell.
You do not need to be a scientist to check something. You need a few good questions and the patience to ask them. This paper is full of those questions.
As always, none of the activities need a phone or an account.

pages.bloopSays: I once thought a picture of a cat in a spacesuit was real. It was not. Let's get better at this together.

inside.title: What research says about spotting fakes

pages.headline: How to check a picture
pages.standfirst: Four questions to ask before you believe, or share, a picture you have found.

art.alt: A diagram of a machine taking in clues at the top and giving out a guess at the bottom.

body.text: Who made it? Look for the name of a person or an organisation you could check.
Where else is it? If something amazing happened, more than one trusted place will usually say so.
Does anything look odd? Hands, writing and shadows are good places to look closely.
How does it make you feel? Pictures made to shock or to rush you deserve a slower look.

pages.friendSays: My magnifier is enormous, but the best tool is a question.

activity.title: Hide a mistake
activity.intro: Draw a picture on the grid with one thing wrong in it. Can a grown up spot it?
steps: Draw something simple, like a house or a face.
Add one mistake, like a window in the sky.
Swap with someone and spot each other's mistake.

pages.headline: Design a fake detector
pages.standfirst: Invent a gadget that helps people check what they see. Start with the person it helps.
pages.friendSays: Mine beeps when a picture has six fingers. It also beeps at gloves. Work in progress.

activity.title: My fake detector
activity.intro: Fill in each box and draw big.

prompts.label: Draw it
prompts.hint: Draw your detector and label every part.

prompts.label: What it checks
prompts.hint: Hands, shadows, writing, where it came from?

prompts.label: What it notices
prompts.hint: What clue does it look for?

prompts.label: What it does back
prompts.hint: A light, a sound, a message?

prompts.label: Test it
prompts.hint: How would you know it works?

tips: Test it on real and pretend pictures you made yourself.
A good detector says how sure it is, not just yes or no.

pages.headline: Kind words travel too
pages.standfirst: A kind message can be checked for one thing only: did it make someone's day?

art.alt: Two homes on two hills joined by a dotted gold line and a row of flowers.

body.text: Checking what is real matters. So does being someone people can trust online. When you share something, you are lending it your name.
If you are not sure something is true, it is fine not to pass it on. Waiting is a kind thing to do.

pages.headline: Was this picture made by a computer?
pages.standfirst: Bloop found a picture of a dog surfing a rainbow. Time for some clues.

art.alt: A diagram of a machine taking in clues at the top and giving out a guess at the bottom.

pages.friendSays: Case closed: no single clue proves it. Lots of clues together make a good guess, and a grown up can help you check.

clues.title: Look at the edges
clues.text: Are there odd blurs or shapes where things meet?

clues.title: Look at the details
clues.text: Hands, teeth, writing and patterns can go wrong.

clues.title: Look for the maker
clues.text: Who posted it first, and do they say how it was made?

clues.title: Look around
clues.text: Does anyone trusted show the same thing?

body.text: An algorithm is a list of steps for solving a problem.[[s23]] Some computers follow steps that make pictures, and some follow steps that recommend what to watch next.[[s22]]

tryThis: Make a picture yourself, then ask a grown up to guess how you made it.
Play Real or Pretend on the next page.

pages.headline: Real or Pretend
pages.standfirst: One player is the Maker, one is the Detective. Can the Detective tell which cards are real?
pages.friendSays: I was the Detective and I said everything was pretend. That is not detecting, apparently.

activity.title: Real or Pretend
setup: Cut out the 12 cards and shuffle them.
The Maker secretly marks some cards REAL and some PRETEND on the back.
rounds: The Detective asks one question about a card.
The Detective says real or pretend, and checks the back.
talk: Which cards fooled you, and why?

tips: Make your own cards from pictures you drew yourself.
